_why: M8b deliverable 6: 'Robots class, canonical link and inlined data on the
transaction route are UNCHANGED — a crawler sees exactly what it saw
before.' Its verification asks for the assertion to be made 'against a
stored baseline so the SEO surface cannot regress silently'.
This is that baseline. It is a stored FILE rather than a constant in the
test because the point is that changing the crawl surface has to be a
deliberate edit to a committed artefact that a reviewer sees in the diff —
a literal inside the assertion would move with the code that broke it.
Recorded from the transaction route as it was BEFORE the debug route
existed: `noindex,follow`, canonical at the transaction's own URL, and the
chain-native payload rendered into the page (§7.2 section 8). The debug
route is `noindex` and canonicalises to the transaction — so this
milestone adds no second indexable copy of the same content, which is the
way a new route most easily damages an existing one.
